solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Answer given by politician originally intended as defence

indicators.note: something done originally comes at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for answer
a Lib is a Liberal politician
the opening letter of intended

explanation.surface: A politician gives a reply that was meant from the start to defend them.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is the plea that the accused was elsewhere, used as a defence in court.

clue.text: Further article on London Symphony Orchestra

indicators.note: on places one thing next to another, here the first piece before the second

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
its standard initials

explanation.surface: Another newspaper piece about the London Symphony Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Also and further are both adverbs meaning in addition or besides.

clue.text: Artist visiting home country

indicators.note: someone visiting is inside another place, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter goes back to visit their native land.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a country in western Asia, formerly Persia.

clue.text: Where you might find turtle up a gum tree?

blocks.note: first meaning: turtle soup is a classic dish, so the turtle sits literally in a bowl of broth
second meaning: a British idiom for being stuck in serious trouble

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures an animal in a tree, but 'up a gum tree' is an idiom for being in a fix.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the soup is informal for being in trouble, and turtle meat famously ends up as soup.

clue.text: Crazy children's game needs new beginning

indicators.note: a new beginning means the first letter of the game's name is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: conkers is a British playground game of smashing horse chestnuts on strings

explanation.surface: A tired playground game is in need of a fresh start.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter leaves the new first letter for the definition to settle: swap the C of CONKERS for B to get BONKERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonkers is British slang for mad or crazy.

clue.text: Banned a poet, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said or told, so we want a word that is spoken alike

blocks.note: a bard is a poet; in non-rhotic speech the two words are said the same

explanation.surface: A writer of verse has been prohibited, so the rumour goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To be barred is to be excluded or prohibited, the same as banned.

clue.text: A number turning up in trap

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: A figure keeps appearing caught in a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A net is a mesh used to catch fish or animals, a kind of trap.

clue.text: Into vice, strangely, leads to expulsion

indicators.note: strangely means in an odd way, so the letters come out in an odd order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Falling oddly into wicked ways gets someone thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: Eviction is the forced removal of a tenant from a property, an expulsion.

clue.text: Guide restraining a girl becoming calmer

indicators.note: restraining means holding something back within limits, so one piece is held inside the other

blocks.note: to steer is to guide
taken as written
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A mentor holding back an excitable young woman helps her settle down.
explanation.definitionFit: Steadier is the comparative of steady, meaning more composed or less agitated.

clue.text: Destroy revival of the arts

indicators.note: a revival brings something back in a new form, so the letters are rebuilt in another order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A campaign to wreck the newly revived arts scene.
explanation.definitionFit: To shatter something is to smash it to pieces, which is to destroy it.

clue.text: Hallucinate when taking ecstasy? That's nonsense

blocks.note: to trip is to hallucinate on drugs
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses the idea of seeing visions on ecstasy as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when taking' looks like a container signal but here just joins the two pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe, literally cow's stomach lining, is informal for worthless talk or rubbish.

clue.text: Rebel cadet somehow becoming famous

indicators.note: somehow says the result is reached by some unexplained route, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rebellious military trainee somehow becomes a household name.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated means widely renowned, a synonym of famous.

clue.text: Sad, unlike Edith Piaf?

blocks.note: surface reading: feeling sorrowful
setter's reading: the French singer's famous song says she regrets nothing, so her opposite is full of regret

explanation.surface: Someone gloomy is being contrasted with the famous French chanteuse.
explanation.walkthrough: Piaf's signature song is 'Non, je ne regrette rien' (No, I regret nothing).
explanation.definitionFit: To be regretful is to feel sorrow or remorse about something, so sad fits.

clue.text: Conservative girl in charge of son's great works

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a lass is a girl
IC stands for in charge
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A Tory girl put in charge of her son's masterpieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of son's is a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Classics are acknowledged masterpieces of literature, art or music.

clue.text: Traitor angered English terribly

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters are scrambled into a poor order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A turncoat has made the English furious.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade is someone who deserts a cause or side, a traitor.

clue.text: Go to ground, unhappy after deception

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other, so the deception word comes first

blocks.note: a lie is a deception
feeling low is feeling unhappy

explanation.surface: A disgraced liar, miserable after being found out, goes into hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie low is to hide away, the idiom matching an animal that goes to ground.

clue.text: Snub Italian gentleman lacking introduction

indicators.note: without its introduction a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for Italian
signore is Italian for a gentleman

explanation.surface: Someone cold-shoulders an Italian gentleman who has not been introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: To snub someone is to ignore them pointedly, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Society girl meeting retired teacher? Rubbish!

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or gone back, so in this down entry the word reads upwards

blocks.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young woman entering high society
pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A debutante bumps into her old schoolmaster, now pensioned off, to which the cry is nonsense!
explanation.definitionFit: Debris is scattered waste or fragments, so it is rubbish in the literal sense.

clue.text: Amorous glances from Dolly perhaps?

blocks.note: surface reading: loving looks cast at someone
setter's reading: Dolly was the famous cloned sheep, so her glances come from that animal's eyes

explanation.surface: Someone called Dolly making eyes at an admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: Dolly reads as a woman's name, but it points to Dolly the sheep cloned in Scotland in 1996.
explanation.definitionFit: Making sheep's eyes is an idiom for gazing at someone with foolish, lovesick longing.

clue.text: King and fool join together

blocks.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A monarch and his court jester team up.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to unite or bond, as a broken bone knits or a team knits together.

clue.text: Lazy celebrity one might say

indicators.note: one might say points to how a word is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: an idol is an adored celebrity

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a famous person is a layabout.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means avoiding work or activity, which is being lazy.

clue.text: Man from Pisa accepted to an extent

indicators.note: to an extent means only partly, so the answer is a run of letters inside the words

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A visitor from Pisa was made welcome, up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac is a man's first name, as in the biblical patriarch or Isaac Newton.

clue.text: Mostly elegant character from Greece

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: chic means stylish or elegant

explanation.surface: A largely stylish figure from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is the twenty-second letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in the written sense.

clue.text: Sophisticated socialist receiving financial penalty

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: a red is a socialist or communist
a fine is a monetary penalty

explanation.surface: A cultured left-winger is landed with a fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined means cultured and elegant in manner, a synonym of sophisticated.

clue.text: Enemy agents sheltering city group

indicators.note: sheltering means keeping something safely inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: spies are agents working for the enemy
EC is the postcode for the City of London

explanation.surface: Hostile operatives hide a cell of city conspirators.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postal district for the City, London's financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A species is a biological group of related organisms that can interbreed.

clue.text: At last minute grabbing time for coffee

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing hold of something, so a letter is taken inside

blocks.note: arriving at the last minute is late
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone rushes in at the last moment to snatch a moment for a coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is an Italian-style coffee made with lots of steamed milk.
